# What the second attempt found

The review gate put `must_fix` at 0.59 against a 0.7 threshold and `severity` most
likely blocking. The record said pass. The gate was right.

## The defect that sent it back

Nothing read `.env.local`. The README said to copy `.env.example` to it, `.env.example`
carried every variable the services and the three providers read, and the secrets
provider's own error said `Set SEEN_SECRET_X in .env.local`. No process ever opened the
file. A developer following the README exactly would set a marketplace credential and
watch the provider say the secret was missing.

`loadLocalEnvironment` now reads it with Node's own parser, so the syntax is the one
`node --env-file` uses rather than a library's dialect of it, and a variable already in
the environment wins: a deployment must not be overridden by a file left in an image,
and after go-live there is no file at all.

## Two more defects that only running it could find

Wiring the loader into `apps/api` and `apps/worker` broke both at boot with
`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on `packages/providers/src/environment`. Lint, typecheck and all
26 tests were green at the time. Node loads a package's TypeScript source directly here,
as ESM, where a relative import has to name a file that exists; `packages/providers` is
the first package in this repository with a second file, so nothing had hit it.
`allowImportingTsExtensions` with `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` is the fix: the
source says `./environment.ts`, which resolves, and tsc rewrites it to `./environment.js`
on emit, which also resolves. `"type": "module"` on the package stops Node parsing the
file twice and saying so on every boot.

Then `PORT=8081` in `.env.local` still did not move the api. The loader defaulted to
`process.cwd()`, and `nest start` runs from `apps/api` while `pnpm --filter` runs from
the package, so it looked for a file that was not there and found nothing, silently. It
now defaults to the repository root, found by walking up to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

Three defects, and the unit tests saw none of them. Each surfaced by starting the thing
and watching it fail.

## Proof

`PORT=8081` in `.env.local`, `pnpm dev`: the api answered on 8081 and 8080 was dead.
With the line removed it is back on 8080. No module errors, no reparse warnings, web
still 200.

One thing the attempt also fixed in the tests themselves: the suite now loads the
developer's real `.env.local`, so the environment tests explicitly clear the names they
assert on. Without that they pass on most machines and fail on the one machine that has
the variable set, which is the worst kind of test to leave behind.
